title: Desmond Spann showed up, picked up a camera and earned a job with the City of Rowlett
excerpt: Nobody asked him to document Rowlett's big moments. He did it anyway, and his initiative turned into a place on city staff.
body:
Some people wait to be asked. Desmond Spann didn't.

If you've been to a Rowlett Chamber event or a community gathering over the past while, there's a good chance Desmond was there with a camera. Without anyone asking him to, he started documenting events around town, capturing the moments he knew were important and worth remembering.

He kept showing up. He offered his services. And photo by photo, event by event, he built a portfolio the old-fashioned way: by taking the initiative and doing the job.

People noticed. Today Desmond is serving Rowlett as a member of the city's staff.

It's a reminder that in a community like ours, showing up still matters. The young people who step in, help out and pay attention to what's happening around them are the ones who end up shaping the town we all share.

The next time you see Desmond at an event, say hello and tell him thanks for helping tell Rowlett's story.
